findings.title: Annual-aggregate thresholds are not modelled for §194J, §194H, §194A, §194D, §194G or §194Q — the engine silently deducts nothing on repeat vendors
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/tds/section_rates.py:110-150 gives only §194C an `aggregate_threshold_paise`; every other section is a bare `single_threshold_paise`. apps/api/domain/tds/tds_computer.py:304-307: `applies = taxable_paise > rule.single_threshold_paise or (rule.aggregate_threshold_paise is not None and fy_total > rule.aggregate_threshold_paise)` — with `aggregate_threshold_paise is None` for 194J/194H/194A/194D/194G/194Q the FY aggregate is never tested. Run in this session: `resolve_tds('194J', 45_000_00, fy_prior_taxable_paise=4_00_000_00, fy='2025-26')` → `applies=False, tds=0`; `resolve_tds('194H', 15_000_00, prior=1_00_000_00)` → 0; `resolve_tds('194Q', 10_00_000_00, prior=1_00_00_000_00)` → 0. §194J's own proviso reads 'the amount of such sum or, as the case may be, the AGGREGATE of the amounts of such sums credited or paid ... during the financial year does not exceed fifty thousand rupees'; §194H, §194A, §194D and §194G are worded the same way, and §194Q charges on purchases 'of the value or aggregate of such value exceeding fifty lakh rupees in any previous year'. The module docstring at section_rates.py:52-56 claims the modelling is 'CONSERVATIVE ... so the tool over-flags rather than silently under-deducts', which is the opposite of what the shape does.
findings.ca_experience: A consultant billed ₹40,000 in April, ₹40,000 in July and ₹40,000 in October under §194J: the platform withholds ZERO on all three, when ₹12,000 was due from the first bill's aggregate crossing. The CA discovers it at year end or when the assessing officer disallows 30% of the ₹1,20,000 under §40(a)(ia) and charges §201(1A) interest at 1%/month from each credit date. Same failure on every commission agent under §194H (₹20,000 FY aggregate) and on every §194Q buyer.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime, Zoho Books and Saral TDS all track the per-deductee per-section FY cumulative and trigger the deduction — and retrospectively deduct on the crossing bill — because that is the only way the proviso can be honoured. Tally's 'TDS Nature of Payment' master carries both the single and the exemption-limit figures.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `aggregate_threshold_paise` to every section whose proviso is an FY aggregate (194A 10_000_00, 194D/194G/194H 20_000_00, 194J 50_000_00, 194Q 50_00_000_00) and keep the single-payment figure only where the statute genuinely is per-payment (194C ₹30,000, 194I ₹50,000 per month, 194B per transaction). `_resolve_bill_resident_tds` already computes `fy_prior` for every section, so the plumbing exists. Decide and encode what happens on the crossing bill: the statute requires TDS on the whole aggregate, so the crossing bill must withhold on `fy_total`, not just on itself.

findings.title: §194Q withholds 0.1% of the whole invoice instead of 0.1% of the sum exceeding ₹50 lakh — a six-fold over-deduction
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/tds/tds_computer.py:317: `tds = taxable_paise * rate_bps // 10000` applied to the full `taxable_paise` for every section including 194Q (`"194Q": TDSSectionRule(50_00_000_00, 10, 10)` at apps/api/domain/tds/section_rates.py:141). §194Q(1) charges 'a sum equal to 0.1 per cent of such sum EXCEEDING fifty lakh rupees'. Run in this session: `resolve_tds('194Q', 60_00_000_00, fy='2025-26')` → ₹6,000 withheld; the statute gives ₹1,000 (0.1% of ₹10 lakh).
findings.ca_experience: On a ₹60 lakh purchase the client withholds ₹6,000 instead of ₹1,000 and short-pays the supplier by ₹5,000. The supplier's 26AS shows a credit that does not match its books, and the buyer's 26Q reports a figure it cannot reconcile to §194Q. The error scales — on a ₹5 crore annual purchase the over-deduction is ~₹45,000.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime and Zoho Books both compute §194Q on the excess over the ₹50 lakh threshold and carry the running cumulative per supplier per FY; ClearTax's TDS module does the same. The identical 'on the excess' rule applies to TCS §206C(1H), which this codebase does not implement at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Give TDSSectionRule a `charges_on_excess: bool` (true for 194Q, and for 206C(1H) when TCS is built) and compute `max(0, fy_total - threshold) * rate_bps // 10000` less what has already been withheld this FY. Add the §194Q(1) proviso's ₹10-crore-turnover precondition on the buyer as a named gap rather than assuming it.

verification.probe: ran resolve_tds("194Q", 60_00_000_00): Rs 6,000 withheld against Rs 1,000 (0.1% of the excess)

findings.title: "Prepare a Return" on /tds/returns cannot work in production — it sends no auth token, and the deductions it looks for carry a NULL financial_year and a differently-formatted quarter
findings.evidence: Three independent breaks on one path. (1) apps/web/lib/data/tds.ts:112-119 and :123-130 — `compute26Q`/`compute24Q` call `fetch(...)` with only `Content-Type`, no `Authorization`; apps/api/routers/tds.py:130 and :214 gate both on `Depends(rbac("tds","compute"))`, and apps/api/core/auth.py:171-175 raises 401 when the Bearer header is absent (the dev fallback at auth.py:153-169 applies only when SUPABASE_URL is unset). Every other call in the same file goes through `authedFetch` (lib/data/tds.ts:135-149). (2) apps/api/services/tds_register_service.py:218-252 — the upsert payload writes `quarter` but never `financial_year`; migration 263 added the column and nothing backfills new rows (apps/api/migrations/263_tds_deductions_financial_year.sql:44-75 backfills existing rows only, no trigger). (3) the register writes `quarter` as `"Q3 2025-26"` (tds_register_service.py:89-96, asserted in apps/api/tests/test_tds_register_follows_the_bill.py:196) while apps/web/app/tds/returns/page.tsx:104 calls `getTDSDeductions(clientId, financialYear, quarter)` with `quarter` of type `TDSQuarter = "Q1"|...` and lib/data/tds.ts:227-233 filters `.eq("financial_year", fy).eq("quarter", quarter)`.
findings.ca_experience: The CA picks a client, FY and quarter, clicks Compute, and gets "No TDS deductions found for this period. Add deductions from the TDS Deductions tab" — even when the client has fifty posted purchase bills with TDS. If they add rows by hand on /tds (which writes quarter as "Q1 (Apr-Jun)") the filter still misses, and if it ever matched, the POST would come back 401 Unauthorized as "26Q compute failed". The one screen labelled 'Prepare a Return' can never produce a return.
findings.market_standard: Saral TDS, Winman TDS and ClearTDS all assemble the quarter from the deduction register with no re-keying, and every one of them ships a working FVU output. This is the core task of a TDS module.
findings.suggested_fix: Switch compute26Q/compute24Q to the file's own `authedFetch`. Write `financial_year` in `sync_for_bill`'s upsert (fy_label(when) already exists in the module). Then delete the browser-side assembly entirely and point the screen at `POST /api/tds/26q/from-books` and `/24q/from-books`, which are already correct and already GL-reconciled — see TDS-05 and TDS-06 for what the browser path also gets wrong.

findings.title: Form 16/16A certificate creation always fails silently against the real database — the UI sends "Form 16A", the CHECK constraint accepts only "16A"
findings.evidence: apps/api/migrations/037_tds_engine.sql:89: `certificate_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (certificate_type IN ('16','16A','16B','16C'))`; no later migration alters it (grep over migrations/*.sql for certificate_type returns only that line). apps/web/app/clients/[id]/compliance/tds/page.tsx:681 seeds the form with `certificate_type: "Form 16A"` and :739-744 offers `<option>Form 16</option><option>Form 16A</option>`. apps/api/routers/tds_workspace.py:561 writes `"certificate_type": body.certificate_type` verbatim. The handler's `except Exception` at tds_workspace.py:586-588 turns the constraint violation into `api_response(False, None, str(e))` — an HTTP 200 — and apps/web/app/clients/[id]/compliance/tds/page.tsx:702-707 (`saveNew`) never inspects the response, it just closes the panel and reloads. Every mock-mode test passes because `_USE_MOCK` writes a dict (tests/test_phase3_tds.py:111 uses "Form 16A"); the only real-Postgres insert, tests/test_gst_tds_schema_drift_pg.py:291, uses '16A'.
findings.ca_experience: The CA fills in the deductee, PAN, FY, section and amount, clicks 'Generate Draft', the panel closes — and the certificate list is unchanged. No error, no toast, nothing in the console the CA would see. They try again, and again. Form 16A tracking simply does not work on the deployed product.
findings.market_standard: Form 16A is generated on TRACES, but Saral TDS, ClearTDS and Winman all maintain the request/download/issue register and bulk-merge the TRACES PDFs per deductee. Here even the register row cannot be created.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise at the router — map 'Form 16'→'16', 'Form 16A'→'16A' — or change the select values. Then stop swallowing DB errors into a 200: `create_certificate` should raise 422 on a constraint violation, and `saveNew` must check `r.success` and surface `r.error`. Add a real-Postgres test that posts the request model the UI actually sends.

findings.title: The /tds page computes TDS in the browser from a hardcoded, stale rate table and writes it straight to tds_deductions, bypassing the engine and rbac()
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/tds/page.tsx:49-61 hardcodes `TDS_SECTIONS` with `194D: 5%` and `194H: 5%` — both cut to 2% by the Finance (No.2) Act 2024 from 01-10-2024, and correctly 200 bps in apps/api/domain/tds/section_rates.py:126,130. The file header (lines 3-16) also cites §194A '₹40,000 bank, ₹5,000 others', the pre-Finance-Act-2025 figures. app/tds/page.tsx:159-171 auto-fills the rate from that table and computes `const tdsPaise = Math.round((grossPaise * tdsRate) / 100)` — no threshold, no §194C aggregate, no §206AA no-PAN floor, and `Math.round` where the backend floors (`tds_computer.py:317` uses `// 10000`). :183-197 and :764-778 then `sb.from("tds_deductions").insert({...})` over PostgREST, so `rbac("tds","compute")` never runs and `TDSComputer.resolve_tds` is never called. CLAUDE.md: 'Zero business logic in the frontend'.
findings.ca_experience: A CA recording a ₹1,00,000 commission under §194H sees the rate auto-fill to 5% and ₹5,000 withheld. The correct figure is 2% / ₹2,000. They have over-deducted ₹3,000 from the payee, and the row lands in the register with `tds_rate_pct = 5.00` and goes onto the 26Q working paper at that rate. A ₹20,000 §194J payment gets 10% withheld even though it is below the ₹50,000 threshold.
findings.market_standard: Every one of Tally, Zoho Books, ClearTax and Saral holds one rate master, updates it by patch each Finance Act, and computes centrally. None of them lets a UI carry its own copy.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `TDS_SECTIONS` with a `listTdsSections(fy)` call (the endpoint exists — routers/tds.py:371, and apps/web/app/accounting/suppliers/page.tsx:186 already does exactly this) and the amount with `computeTdsAmount({section, payment_amount_paise, pan, fy})` (routers/tds.py:335). Move the insert behind a POST endpoint so rbac and the register's own rules apply. Add a lint/test that fails on any TDS rate literal under apps/web.

findings.title: On a 26Q working paper every deductee row is stamped with the first challan found for its section, and deposits are apportioned by weight rather than matched to the month
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/tds_return_service.py:215: `matching_challan = next((c for c in challans if (c.get("section") or "") == section), None)` — the first challan in an unordered PostgREST result (`_deposited_challans` at :150-153 issues no `.order()`). A quarter always has three monthly deposits under Rule 30 (7 May, 7 Jun, 7 Jul for Q1), all carrying the same section, so all three months' deductees are labelled with whichever one comes back first. Separately, :200-209 apportions `min(deposited_total, sum(weights))` across the section's bills by largest-remainder, so a bill fully deposited in April is shown as partly deposited whenever the quarter as a whole is short.
findings.ca_experience: The CA downloads the Q1 26Q working paper to key into the RPU and finds every June deductee pointing at the April challan's BSR code and serial. The FVU cross-checks deductee rows against the challan they sit under, so the statement is rejected — or worse, accepted with the wrong challan and every one of those deductees' 26AS entries booked 'U' (unmatched), which the deductees then chase the client about. The 'deposited' column against each vendor is a proportion, not what was actually paid for that vendor.
findings.market_standard: In the NSDL RPU the deductee annexure is physically nested under its challan; Saral TDS, Winman and ClearTDS all require the deduction to be tagged to a specific challan, and refuse to build the file until every deduction is mapped. Tally's 'TDS Challan Reconciliation' does the same.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `challan_id` FK on `tds_deductions` (migration 037 already added `tds_return_id`; the challan link was the one it named and did not create) and a challan-mapping screen. Failing that, match a bill to the challan whose deposit period covers the bill's month — deduction month → deposit due 7th of the next month, March → 30 April — and order the challan query deterministically.

findings.title: §194IA is offered in the vendor TDS-section dropdown but is unknown to the engine — every bill for such a vendor is refused with a 422
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/clients/[id]/purchases/page.tsx:233 offers `{ value: "194IA", label: "194IA — Purchase of Immovable Property (1%)" }` and :246 maps it to 100 bps; apps/api/routers/purchase_bills.py:33 has the same stale default map. But `_SECTIONS_2025_26` (apps/api/domain/tds/section_rates.py:110-150) has no 194IA entry, so `resolve_tds` raises `ValueError("Unknown TDS section '194IA'")` (tds_computer.py:301), which purchase_bills.py:346-347 turns into `HTTPException(422, str(ve))`. Verified in this session: `resolve_tds('194IA', 60_00_000_00, fy='2025-26')` → `Unknown TDS section '194IA'`.
findings.ca_experience: A CA sets a property vendor to §194IA, then tries to book the purchase bill and gets 'Unknown TDS section 194IA'. The bill cannot be saved at all until they change the section to something the engine happens to know. The same dropdown also shows 194D and 194H at 5% (see TDS-05) and writes `tds_rate_bps` that the backend then ignores (TDS-13).
findings.market_standard: §194IA (1% on immovable property over ₹50 lakh, Form 26QB, Form 16B) is a standard section in every Indian TDS product. It also files on a challan-cum-statement (26QB) rather than 26Q, which is why it needs its own treatment rather than a registry row.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove 194IA from the dropdown with a note that 26QB is not supported, or add it properly: registry entry, ₹50 lakh threshold on the consideration or stamp-duty value (whichever is higher, from FY 2019-20), and a 26QB path separate from 26Q. Generate the frontend's section list from `GET /api/tds/sections` so the two can never diverge again.

findings.title: No §201(1A) interest and no §234E late fee are computed anywhere a CA can use them
findings.evidence: grep across apps/api for '201(1A)' finds only prose: apps/api/domain/ai_insight_service.py:270, apps/api/domain/tds/residency.py:148, apps/api/services/compliance_engine.py:272,297, apps/api/routers/payroll.py:732. '234E' appears only inside the filing walk-through, apps/api/services/filing_demo/tds_return.py:32-33,198-216, which computes `min(days_late * 200_00, deducted)` for display in a demo that transmits nothing. `tds_challans` has an `interest_paise` and `penalty_paise` column (migrations/037_tds_engine.sql:66-68) and apps/api/routers/tds_workspace.py:275-290 (`create_challan`) never populates them — it books the whole amount as pure TDS (`"tds_paise": body.amount_paise, "total_paise": body.amount_paise`).
findings.ca_experience: A client deducted ₹80,000 in June and deposited it on 20 August. The CA has to work out on paper that §201(1A)(ii) charges 1.5% per month or part from the DATE OF DEDUCTION (not the due date) — three part-months, ₹3,600 — and add it to the challan by hand under the right minor head. The platform neither warns that the deposit is late nor tells them the number. Same for the ₹200/day §234E fee, which must be paid before the statement can be filed at all.
findings.market_standard: Saral TDS, Winman TDS, ClearTDS and TaxCloud all compute §201(1A) interest per deduction from the deduction date and §234E from the Rule 31A due date, and print both onto the challan 281 worksheet. Tally Prime shows interest on its 'TDS Outstanding' report.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `domain/tds/interest.py` with two pure functions — `interest_201_1a(deducted_on, deposited_on, amount_paise, failure: 'not_deducted'|'not_deposited')` at 1%/1.5% per month or part, and `fee_234e(due_date, filed_on, tds_paise)` capped at the TDS — with unit tests, and surface both on the challan create screen and the return screen. Both are pure arithmetic over dates the system already holds.

findings.title: There is no 27Q return builder — non-resident deductions are computed, registered and then deliberately excluded from 26Q with nothing to file them on
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/tds_return_service.py:181-187 filters non-resident bills out of 26Q and reports them at :275-287 as `excluded_non_resident` with the reason 'Payments to a non-resident are reported on Form 27Q under Rule 31A(4)(b), not on 26Q.' No 27Q builder exists: grep for '27Q' across apps/api/routers and apps/api/services finds only the `return_type` filter validation at routers/tds.py:469-473 and the residency constants. The register does write full 27Q rows — country, TIN, surcharge, cess, non-deduction reason (services/tds_register_service.py:237-251) — and the compliance calendar even generates the 27Q deadline (services/compliance_obligation_service.py:196-199). The service docstring at tds_return_service.py:29-31 says 'There is no 27Q counterpart to build it into: s.195 ... is not modelled anywhere in this codebase' — which is now out of date, since domain/tds/section_195.py does rate it.
findings.ca_experience: A client pays a Singapore consultant. The platform correctly refuses §194J, applies §195 with surcharge and cess, records the TRC/10F/no-PE facts and stores a complete 27Q register row. Then the CA gets a calendar reminder for 27Q Q2 and there is no screen and no endpoint that will assemble it. They rebuild the statement by hand from the deduction list.
findings.market_standard: 27Q is a standard output of Saral TDS, Winman TDS and ClearTDS, including the deductee country, TIN, nature-of-remittance code, rate, surcharge, cess and the 15CA/15CB cross-reference.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `tds_27q_from_books` beside the existing 26Q builder, sourced from `tds_deductions` rows with `return_type='27Q'` (which already carry country_of_residence, deductee_tin, surcharge_paise, cess_paise and non_deduction_reason) rather than from purchase_bills, and reconcile it to the same TDS Payable control. Wire it to the existing return-type selector on the compliance TDS screen.

findings.title: TCS (§206C(1H)/(1F)/(1G), Form 27EQ, Form 27D) does not exist — only a rate row nobody reads
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/tds/section_rates.py:142-149 carries `"206C": TDSSectionRule(0, 10, 10)` with its own comment: 'NOT wired to any computation anywhere in this codebase — confirmed zero readers ... do not assume TCS is an implemented feature because a rate exists here.' grep for 'tcs' in apps/api/routers/sales_invoices.py and routers/receipts.py returns nothing; the only other hits are the `TCS_RETURN` task-type enums in migrations/001, 002 and 006 and the `27EQ` label in domain/tds/vocabulary.py:96,100. `tds_returns.return_type` and `tds_deductions.return_type` both allow '27EQ' (migrations/037:13, 014:188) and nothing ever writes it.
findings.ca_experience: An SME client selling over ₹50 lakh to one buyer must collect 0.1% TCS under §206C(1H), show it on the invoice, deposit it, file 27EQ quarterly and issue Form 27D. None of that is possible here — the CA runs it in Tally or a spreadsheet, which is exactly the 'one platform' claim breaking. A client selling a motor vehicle over ₹10 lakh (§206C(1F)) or remitting under LRS (§206C(1G)) has the same problem.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime computes TCS on the invoice line and files 27EQ; Zoho Books supports 206C(1H); Saral and Winman both ship 27EQ and Form 27D. TCS is table stakes for any product claiming to replace Tally for a trading SME.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope it as its own build: a TCS nature master (1H/1F/1G/scrap/timber), collection on the sales invoice at the point of receipt (206C(1H) is collection-on-receipt, not on invoice), a `tcs_collections` register mirroring `tds_deductions`, the 27EQ statement, and Form 27D. Note that §206C(1H) charges on the receipt EXCEEDING ₹50 lakh — the same excess rule as TDS-02.

findings.title: tds_deductions and tds_returns are written directly from the browser with no role check, and the test that exists to catch exactly this misses them
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/tds/page.tsx:183 and :764 `sb.from("tds_deductions").insert({...})`; apps/web/lib/data/tds.ts:282-305 `sb.from("tds_returns").upsert({...})`. The RLS on both is `FOR ALL USING (firm_id = get_my_firm_id())` with no role predicate and a blanket grant (apps/api/migrations/014_complete_missing_tables.sql:196-200; migrations/037_tds_engine.sql:145-151), so any authenticated firm member — Reviewer included — can insert, amend or delete a statutory deduction row or a TDS return. apps/api/tests/test_direct_write_tables_are_role_guarded.py:66 declares `AWAITING_DECISION: dict[str,str] = {}` with the comment 'Empty: every table the browser writes now carries a role rule'. It does not: the scan regex at :90 caps the tail at `{0,400}?` characters, and I measured 466 characters between `.from("tds_deductions")` and the statement's `;` in app/tds/page.tsx — so the match never reaches `.insert(`. Reproduced in this session: running the module's own `_direct_write_tables()` returns 21 tables and none of them is a tds_* table, while `.insert(` appears twice in that file.
findings.ca_experience: Not visible to a CA until it matters: a Reviewer (read-only by design in core/permissions.py's Partner > Manager > Executive > Reviewer > Client ladder) can delete a filed quarter's deduction rows or flip a return's stored totals, and there is no audit_log entry because log_event only runs on the API path. The backlog document the team relies on says the hole does not exist.
findings.market_standard: Not a market-comparison point — it is an internal control question. Tally's user roles and Zoho's roles both gate voucher and return edits by role.
findings.suggested_fix: Two fixes, both needed. Raise or remove the 400-character cap in the scan (or match `.from("x")` and `.insert|upsert|update|delete` within the same statement by brace-balancing) and re-run it — expect several tables to appear. Then either move both writes behind API endpoints (POST /api/tds-workspace/deductions exists in spirit; the returns POST already exists at routers/tds_workspace.py:354) or add role-aware write policies for tds_deductions and tds_returns in the 260/261 style.

findings.title: The compliance calendar has no 24Q filing deadline and no monthly non-salary TDS deposit deadline — and a docstring asserts otherwise
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/compliance_obligation_service.py:190-200 (`_tds_obligations`) emits only `TDS26Q` and, conditionally, `TDS27Q`. grep for '24Q' across compliance_obligation_service.py and compliance_engine.py returns exactly one hit — the docstring at compliance_obligation_service.py:301 that says 'THE 24Q RETURN IS NOT HERE EITHER — it is already emitted by _tds_obligations, quarterly, for a TDS engagement.' It is not. Separately, the only TDS deposit obligation is `TDS_SALARY_DEPOSIT`, generated from payroll (`_payroll_obligations` at :307-315 with `_PAYROLL_OBLIGATION_TYPE` at :320-324); there is no monthly obligation for the vendor/26Q side, even though `compliance_engine.tds_deposit_due_date` (services/compliance_engine.py:292-306) computes the correct 7th-of-next-month / 30-April-for-March rule and would serve it unchanged.
findings.ca_experience: A CA running payroll for a client sees EPF, ESI and salary-TDS deposit reminders every month — but never a 24Q filing reminder for 31 Jul / 31 Oct / 31 Jan / 31 May, so the ₹200/day §234E fee accrues silently. A client with only vendor TDS gets a 26Q quarterly reminder but no monthly 'deposit by the 7th' reminder, so §201(1A) interest at 1.5%/month accrues on every late deposit.
findings.market_standard: Every Indian practice-management tool (Winman, Saral, CompuOffice, and Zoho Practice) puts the monthly TDS deposit and the quarterly 24Q/26Q/27Q/27EQ filing on the compliance calendar as separate items — that calendar is the reason CAs buy the tool.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `TDS24Q` to `_tds_obligations`, conditional on the client having a payroll engagement or a client_statutory_identity TAN, and add a `TDS_VENDOR_DEPOSIT` monthly obligation driven by `compliance_engine.tds_deposit_due_date`, conditional on the client having any `tds_deductions` row (or any TDS-applicable vendor). Fix the docstring at :301 either way — it is currently load-bearing misinformation.

findings.title: No §197 lower-deduction certificate anywhere, and vendors.tds_rate_bps is captured, displayed and then ignored by the engine
findings.evidence: `vendors` has `tds_rate_bps` (apps/api/migrations/049_customer_vendor_master.sql:60) and no §197 certificate number, certificate rate or validity period; migrations 308/309 added residency and §195 fields but nothing for §197. apps/api/routers/purchase_bills.py:283-347 (`_resolve_bill_resident_tds`) never reads `vendor.get("tds_rate_bps")` — the rate comes only from `tds_rates_for(fy).sections[section]`. Yet apps/web/components/purchases/PurchaseBillEditor.tsx:335-336 previews `estimateForeignTds(estBaseTaxable, selectedVendor.tds_rate_bps ?? 0)` and :592 labels it `TDS §{section} @ {(tds_rate_bps/100)}%`, and apps/web/lib/imports/mappers.ts:146 makes 'TDS Rate %' an import column described as 'required if TDS applicable'. `is_lower_deduction` / `lower_deduction_cert` exist as columns (apps/api/migrations/037_tds_engine.sql:48-49) and as request fields (routers/tds.py:58-59) but nothing sets or computes from them.
findings.ca_experience: A vendor produces a §197 certificate allowing deduction at 2% instead of 10%. The CA sets the vendor's TDS rate to 2%, sees the bill preview show ₹2,000 on a ₹1,00,000 bill — and the saved bill withholds ₹10,000. They have over-deducted ₹8,000 against a valid certificate, and the vendor now has to claim a refund. There is nowhere to record the certificate number, its validity dates or its ceiling amount, so nothing tracks when it expires or when the certified amount is exhausted.
findings.market_standard: Saral TDS, Winman and ClearTDS all hold a §197/§197A certificate master per deductee with number, rate, validity period and the certified ceiling, apply it automatically, stop applying it when the ceiling is consumed, and report the certificate number in the 26Q deductee annexure (which the FVU requires when a below-normal rate is used). Tally Prime has the same in its 'Lower Deduction' TDS master.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a certificate table (deductee, section, certificate no, rate_bps, valid_from, valid_to, ceiling_paise, consumed_paise) and have `resolve_tds` take an optional certificate and use `min(section_rate, certificate_rate)` while the certificate is live and unexhausted, populating `is_lower_deduction`/`lower_deduction_cert` on the register row. Until then, either make the backend honour `vendors.tds_rate_bps` or remove it from the vendor form and the importer so the CA is not shown a rate that does nothing.

findings.title: The purchase-bill editor previews a TDS figure the backend will not compute — no threshold, no §206AA, no §195 surcharge and cess
findings.evidence: apps/web/components/purchases/PurchaseBillEditor.tsx:335-340 computes `tdsPaise` in the browser via `estimateForeignTds(baseTaxable, vendor.tds_rate_bps)` (apps/web/lib/services/currencyPreview.ts:27-29, `Math.floor(base * bps / 10000)`) and subtracts it to show net payable. The backend path (apps/api/routers/purchase_bills.py:531-559) instead branches on residency: a non-resident goes through `_resolve_bill_section_195` (:349-397) which adds surcharge and cess and may raise a 422 refusal, and a resident goes through `resolve_tds` which applies the section threshold and the §206AA floor. None of those inputs is available to the preview.
findings.ca_experience: A CA entering a ₹20,000 §194J bill sees 'TDS §194J @ 10.0% — ₹2,000' and a net payable of ₹18,000 in the editor, then saves and the bill records ₹0 TDS (below the ₹50,000 threshold) and ₹20,000 payable. For a foreign vendor the preview shows the resident section and rate the vendor still carries, and saving either produces a completely different number (base + surcharge + cess) or fails outright with a §195 refusal the editor gave no hint of.
findings.market_standard: Tally and Zoho compute the withheld amount server-side and show the same number in the voucher preview and after saving. A preview that disagrees with the saved document is the thing a CA loses trust in first.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the local estimate with a debounced call to `POST /api/tds/compute-amount` (routers/tds.py:335 — it already takes the PAN and derives is_company and §206AA), and for a non-resident vendor show the §195 resolution or its refusal rather than a resident-section rate. apps/web/app/accounting/suppliers/page.tsx:135-145 already does exactly this and is the pattern to copy.

findings.title: The /tds screen's Challans tab never saves anything, and its Returns and Certificates tabs read columns and status values that do not exist
findings.evidence: Challans: apps/web/app/tds/page.tsx:290-317 (`AddChallanModal`) calls `onAdded({...})` and :739 wires that to `setChallans(prev => [c, ...prev])` — nothing writes `tds_challans`; `challans` is initialised empty at :387 and never loaded. The working endpoint `POST /api/tds-workspace/challans` (apps/api/routers/tds_workspace.py:261) is never called from this page. Certificates: :720-723 render `c.period` and `formatPaise(c.amount_paise)`, but `tds_certificates` has `financial_year`/`quarter` and `tds_deducted_paise` (apps/api/migrations/037_tds_engine.sql:92-98) — no `period`, no `amount_paise`. Returns: :685-688 count `returns.filter(r => r.status === s)` for s in `"Pending"|"Filed"|"Overdue"` while the CHECK stores `'pending','prepared','ca_approved','filed','revised'` (migrations/037:24-25); `TDSReturn` at :110-117 also names `form_type`, `fy` and `filed_date` against real columns `return_type`, `financial_year`, `filed_at`.
findings.ca_experience: The CA enters a Challan 281 — BSR code, date, serial, amount — it appears in the list, they navigate away and it is gone. Permanently, with no error. The Certificates tab shows blank periods and an empty/NaN TDS amount for every certificate. The Returns tab's three counters read 0 / 0 / 0 no matter how many returns exist.
findings.market_standard: Challan entry and challan-to-deduction mapping is the daily work in Saral TDS and ClearTDS; nothing there is ephemeral.
findings.suggested_fix: Point `AddChallanModal` at `POST /api/tds-workspace/challans` and load the list from `GET /api/tds-workspace/challans`. Fix the certificate and return field names against migration 037 and lower-case the status vocabulary (apps/web/app/clients/[id]/compliance/tds/page.tsx:36-43 already has the right map). Consider retiring /tds entirely in favour of the per-client compliance/tds screen, which is the one that calls the real API.

findings.title: No FVU/RPU-format output and no correction-statement support — the only export is a JSON blob
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/data/tds.ts:308-316 (`downloadTDSJSON`) writes `JSON.stringify(payload)` to a `.json` file. `tds_returns.fvu_json` is JSONB (apps/api/migrations/037_tds_engine.sql:31) and holds the same object; nothing produces the NSDL file-format text file the RPU/FVU consumes. The only other export is the 24Q CSV working paper (apps/api/domain/payroll/form24q.py:300-330), which labels itself 'Not an FVU file; not filed'. `tds_returns.status` allows 'revised' (migrations/037:24) but apps/api/routers/tds_workspace.py:432 restricts the allowed transitions to `{"pending","prepared","ca_approved","filed"}`, so a return can never be moved to revised, and nothing models a correction statement's C1/C2/C3/C4/C5 types or the original PRN it corrects.
findings.ca_experience: Having prepared the quarter, the CA downloads a JSON file the RPU cannot read and re-keys every deductee into the free NSDL RPU by hand — which is the whole job the software was supposed to remove. When TRACES raises a short-deduction default a month later, there is no way to prepare the correction statement here at all.
findings.market_standard: Saral TDS, Winman TDS, ClearTDS and TaxCloud all produce the FVU-ready text file directly and all handle correction statements against the original PRN, including consolidated-file import from TRACES. This is the single feature that makes a TDS product purchasable.
findings.suggested_fix: Generate the NSDL file-format text (the record layout is published per FY and per form) from the existing payload, and validate against the CSI file. Model corrections as a return row carrying `original_prn` and a correction type. Both are large; the FVU writer is the one that decides whether a CA would buy this module.

findings.title: For FY 2026-27 the 26Q payload names the form 140 while every deductee line still cites a 1961-Act section — the exact mistake the vocabulary module exists to prevent
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/tds_return_service.py:247 translates the form (`statement_form(RESIDENT_NON_SALARY, fy_label=fy)` → '140' for 2026-27) but :263 emits `"section": d.section` untranslated, and the deductee's section came straight off `b.get("tds_section")` at :219. apps/api/routers/tds.py:176-177 and :191 do the same. Contrast apps/api/domain/payroll/form24q.py:164-165, which does it right: `vocab = vocabulary.vocabulary_for(financial_year); section = vocab.section(SECTION_192)`. apps/api/domain/tds/vocabulary.py:312-314 warns explicitly: 'naming a statement Form 138 and then citing s. 192 on its lines is exactly the mistake this module exists to prevent, and it is only possible if the two are resolved separately.'
findings.ca_experience: A CA preparing a FY 2026-27 quarter gets a working paper headed 'Form 140' whose every line says 194J or 194C — sections that no longer exist under the Income-tax Act 2025, where the whole 194-series is s. 393(1). Keyed into the portal that is a processing error and a correction statement. (In practice the CA is blocked earlier by the s.393 payment-code gap the module honestly reports, so this is caught — but by the wrong safety net.)
findings.market_standard: Not yet a market comparison — the 2025-Act renumbering is new to everyone. What is comparable is that the 24Q path here already does it correctly, so the 26Q path is inconsistent with its own codebase.
findings.suggested_fix: In `tds_26q_from_books` and in `routers/tds.py`'s two compute handlers, resolve one `Vocabulary` for the period and pass every deductee's section through `vocab.section(...)`, exactly as form24q.py:164-165 does. Add the parity assertion to the vocabulary test so a future emission point cannot skip it.

findings.title: Saving a computed FY 2026-27 return violates the tds_returns CHECK constraint, because the payload's form is now '140'/'138'
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/data/tds.ts:284-287 writes `return_type: payload.form` into `tds_returns`; `TDSReturnPayload.form` is typed `"24Q" | "26Q"` at lib/data/tds.ts:77 but the backend now returns whatever `statement_form` gives for the period (apps/api/routers/tds.py:176-177, :258-259) — '140' for a FY 2026-27 26Q and '138' for a 24Q. `tds_returns.return_type` CHECKs `IN ('24Q','26Q','27Q','27EQ')` (apps/api/migrations/037_tds_engine.sql:12).
findings.ca_experience: From FY 2026-27 onward, 'Save' on a prepared return fails with a Postgres check-constraint error the screen surfaces as a raw message. (Today's other breaks on that screen — TDS-03 — mean the CA never reaches this point, which is why nothing has caught it.)
findings.market_standard: n/a — an internal consistency defect introduced by the vocabulary fork.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the stored `return_type` as the routing key ('26Q'/'24Q') — which is exactly the rule `tds_register_service.py:240-247` already articulates for `tds_deductions` — and derive the display form from the period. Widen the TypeScript type to `string` and stop treating the display name as an identifier.

findings.title: The 26AS parser mislabels Part B (TCS) as TDS and Part D (refunds) as self-assessment tax, and nothing filters non-TDS parts out before matching
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/income_tax/form26as_service.py:186-194: `mapping = {"A": "tds_salary", "B": "tds_other", "C": "advance_tax", "D": "self_assessment", "F": "tds_other"}`. In Form 26AS, Part B is TCS collected, Part C is tax paid other than TDS/TCS, Part D is DETAILS OF PAID REFUND, and Part F is TDS on sale of immovable property (buyer's view). Then `_entries_from_records` (:324-337) converts every parsed record into a `Form26ASEntry` with no filter on `part` or `record_type`, and `run_reconciliation` (:558-560) feeds all of them into `_m.reconcile`, whose totals (`total_26as_paise` at domain/income_tax/form26as_matcher.py:431) sum every entry.
findings.ca_experience: A CA pastes a full 26AS. Refund rows from Part D and advance-tax rows from Part C are matched against the client's TDS-receivable credits, come back as 'missing in books', and inflate 'Total TDS per 26AS'. The variance figure the whole screen is built around — and the AI insight it triggers (:454-464) — is wrong, and the CA chases credits that were never TDS.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax's 26AS/AIS import and TaxCloud both parse 26AS by part and keep TDS, TCS, advance tax, self-assessment tax and refunds in separate buckets, because they feed different schedules of the ITR.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the part→record_type map (B→tcs, D→refund, and add A1 for 15G/15H, A2/F for 194-IA), and filter `_entries_from_records` to the TDS/TCS record types only, reporting the other parts separately. Confidence is medium only because the 26AS part layout is quoted from knowledge, not from a specimen in this repo — verify against a real statement before changing the map.

findings.title: The 26AS pipeline accepts only pasted tab/pipe-delimited text and offers no current-year option — a real TRACES download will not parse
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/income_tax/form26as_service.py:132-183 (`parse_26as_text`) splits each line on `\t|\|`, requires at least 5 columns, and reads deductor name, TAN, date, amount, TDS and booking status from fixed positions 1-6; anything else is silently dropped at :182 (`_logger.debug("Skipping unparseable line")`). There is no PDF path — `form_26as_uploads.document_id` exists (routers/form_26as.py:47) but `parse_upload` takes `raw_text` from the request body (:50-51, :99). Separately apps/web/app/clients/[id]/tax/26as/page.tsx:9 hardcodes `FY_OPTIONS = ["2025-26", "2024-25", "2023-24"]`; today is 07-09-2026, so FY 2026-27 cannot be selected at all.
findings.ca_experience: The CA downloads 26AS from TRACES as a PDF (or the password-protected text file), pastes it in, and gets '0 records parsed' with no indication of why — the file is neither tab nor pipe delimited and its columns are not in those positions. And a CA working on the current year finds their FY is not in the dropdown.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax and TaxCloud both ingest the TRACES 26AS text file and the AIS/TIS JSON directly, handling the password and the column layout; Winman imports 26AS into the ITR. Nobody asks the CA to reformat the statement into tab-delimited text first.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the FY list from the clock (there is already `currentFinancialYearLabel` in apps/web/lib/dateMath). For the parser, accept the actual TRACES text export (fixed-width and multi-line rows) and report unparsed lines back to the CA rather than logging at debug; AIS/TIS JSON import is the bigger prize and is a separate build.

findings.title: The TDS workspace's 26AS comparison keys on (PAN, section) in a dict, so multiple deductions for one deductee under one section collapse to a single row
findings.evidence: apps/api/routers/tds_workspace.py:623-643: `form26as_keys = {(e.get("pan",""), e.get("section","")): e for e in form26as_entries}` — a dict comprehension, so with three quarterly 26AS rows for one vendor under §194J only the last survives. Every book deduction with that key is then compared against that one entry, so N book rows can all 'match' one 26AS row, or all report the same variance. The docstring at :601-604 is honest that 'NOTHING is read from the database', but the matcher itself is a second, weaker implementation sitting beside the good one in apps/api/domain/income_tax/form26as_matcher.py (four-pass, identity-first, one-to-one, consuming matched credits — :312-433).
findings.ca_experience: A CA checking the TDS their client deducted from a vendor against the vendor's 26AS uploads twelve monthly deductions and four quarterly 26AS rows for the same PAN and section, and gets a reconciliation that says 'matched' or reports one amount variance that is arithmetic nonsense — the counts in the summary do not add up to the rows on either side.
findings.market_standard: Tally's TDS reconciliation and ClearTDS both match at challan/deductee-row granularity, not by collapsing a PAN+section key.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the inline matcher and route this endpoint through `domain/income_tax/form26as_matcher.reconcile`, which is already pure, one-to-one and tested (apps/api/tests/test_form26as_reconciliation.py). The two directions differ only in which side is which; the passes and the consumption rule are the same.

findings.title: §194J's 2% technical-services rate and §194I's 2% plant-and-machinery rate are not modelled — both over-deduct at 10%
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/tds/section_rates.py:133-135: `"194I": TDSSectionRule(50_000_00, 1000, 1000)` and `"194J": TDSSectionRule(50_000_00, 1000, 1000)`. The module docstring acknowledges the 194J case at :64-65 ('Fees for technical services / call centres are 2% — not separately modelled') but not the 194I one. §194J(1)(ba) charges 2% on fees for technical services (other than professional services), on royalty for cinematographic films, and for a payee whose business is operating a call centre; §194I(a) charges 2% on rent for plant, machinery or equipment against §194I(b)'s 10% for land, building or furniture.
findings.ca_experience: A client renting equipment or a generator pays 10% instead of 2% — on ₹10 lakh of annual equipment rent that is ₹80,000 of the vendor's cash withheld that should not have been, recoverable only when the vendor files. Same for an IT-support or call-centre vendor billed under §194J. There is no way for the CA to override it, because vendors.tds_rate_bps is ignored (TDS-13).
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime's 'Nature of Payment' master distinguishes 194J-professional from 194J-technical and 194I-land/building from 194I-plant/machinery, as do Saral and Winman — the FVU itself requires the sub-section code on the deductee row.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the registry key by nature — '194I(a)'/'194I(b)' and '194J(a)'/'194J(ba)' — or add a `nature` dimension to TDSSectionRule, and put the choice on the vendor master beside the section. The FVU's own section codes already make this distinction, so it will be needed for TDS-16 anyway.

findings.title: Eight commonly-used TDS sections are absent from the registry, including §194T on payments to partners, live since 01-04-2025
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/tds/section_rates.py:110-150 holds 192, 193, 194, 194A, 194B, 194C, 194D, 194G, 194H, 194I, 194J, 194K, 194LA, 194Q and a dead 206C entry. grep across apps/api for '194T', '194R', '194S', '194IB', '194M', '194N', '194O' returns no registry entry (only a passing mention of §194S in apps/api/domain/income_tax/capital_gains_engine.py:206 and §194IA in the stale default map at routers/purchase_bills.py:33). §194T — TDS at 10% on salary, remuneration, commission, bonus or interest paid by a firm to a partner above ₹20,000 — was inserted by the Finance (No. 2) Act 2024 with effect from 01-04-2025 and is therefore live for the whole of FY 2025-26.
findings.ca_experience: Every partnership-firm and LLP client this platform serves — and the owner's own market is CA firms serving SMEs, where the LLP and partnership are the commonest forms — has to deduct §194T on partner remuneration and interest from FY 2025-26. The platform cannot record it, cannot compute it and will not put it on the 26Q. The CA does it outside the product. §194R (benefits/perquisites, 10% over ₹20,000) and §194S (VDA, 1%) are the same story.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime added §194T in its FY 2025-26 release; Saral, Winman and ClearTDS all ship the full Chapter XVII-B section list. A section master that stops at fifteen sections is the first thing a CA notices.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 194T (₹20,000, 10%), 194R (₹20,000, 10%), 194S, 194M (₹50 lakh, 5%), 194N (cash withdrawal), 194O (e-commerce, 0.1% since 01-10-2024), 194IB (₹50,000/month, 2% since 01-10-2024) and 194IA — with a note on each of which are challan-cum-statement forms (26QB/26QC/26QD) rather than 26Q rows, since those need a different return path. Verify each rate and threshold against the Finance Act before adding; the registry's `verified` flag exists for exactly this.

findings.title: §206AB is implemented and unit-tested as current law, but was omitted by the Finance Act 2025 with effect from 01-04-2025
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/tds/tds_validator.py:40-48 `is_higher_rate_applicable(pan, is_non_filer, base_rate)` returns `max(base_rate*2, 5.0)`, documented as 'IT Act Section 206AB: non-filers (ITR not filed for last 2 years)'. apps/api/tests/test_tds_engine.py:327-338 asserts that behaviour in three tests. apps/api/domain/tds/tds_computer.py:7 lists §206AB in the module header as a supported rule. The function is FY-blind — it takes no `fy` parameter, unlike its neighbour `applicable_rate` at :26-38 which does. grep confirms no production caller: the only hits for '206AB' across apps/api and apps/web are the validator, the computer's docstring and that test file.
findings.ca_experience: No wrong number reaches a CA today, because nothing calls the function. The risk is the reverse: the code and its tests present a repealed provision as current, so a future 'wire up 206AB' task would double every rate for a non-filer in a year where the section no longer exists — and CLAUDE.md's own annual-maintenance discipline would not catch it, because §206AB is not on the list of FY-versioned registries.
findings.market_standard: Compliance Check for §206AB was withdrawn on the income-tax portal after the omission; Tally, Saral and ClearTDS all removed the non-filer higher-rate logic for FY 2025-26 onwards.
findings.suggested_fix: Either delete the function and its three tests, or give it an `fy` parameter that returns `base_rate` unchanged for FY 2025-26 onward with the omission cited, and keep it for belated FY 2024-25 work. Confidence is medium because the omission is quoted from knowledge of the Finance Act 2025, not from a source in this repo — confirm before deleting, since §206AB does still govern periods up to 31-03-2025.

findings.title: Form 15CA cannot be recorded against a foreign remittance, so the gap the engine raises can never be cleared
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/tds_register_service.py:213-214 raises `GAP_FORM_15CA_NOT_RECORDED` whenever `is_195 and not (bill.get("form_15ca_ack_no") or "").strip()`. The backend accepts the field on the bill payload (apps/api/routers/purchase_bills.py:780, :826). grep for 'form_15ca' across all of apps/web returns nothing — no input, no display, no column in the bill editor or the bill drawer. The gap message (domain/tds/residency.py:228-232) tells the CA to 'record the acknowledgement number on the bill', which no screen allows.
findings.ca_experience: Every single §195 bill reports the statutory gap 'No Form 15CA acknowledgement is recorded against this remittance', permanently, with no way to act on it. A gap that always fires and cannot be cleared trains the CA to ignore the gap list — which then hides the residency and no-PE gaps that do matter.
findings.market_standard: 15CA/15CB is filed on the e-filing portal; but ClearTax and the foreign-remittance modules of the larger practice suites track the acknowledgement number per remittance and flag the ones that left without it. A tracker, not a filer, is the right scope here and matches this codebase's own never-auto-submit rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `form_15ca_ack_no` input to the purchase-bill editor, shown only when the vendor is a non-resident, and display it on the bill drawer. One field closes a gap the whole §195 pipeline currently reports on every row.

findings.title: §195 surcharge picks the wrong ladder and the wrong 'other sums' rate for a non-resident firm, LLP or co-operative society
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/tds/section_195.py:105-121 chooses between exactly two ladders — `surcharge_foreign_company` (2% over ₹1 crore, 5% over ₹10 crore) and `surcharge_non_corporate` (10/15/25/37) — on the boolean `is_company`, which apps/api/routers/purchase_bills.py:376 derives from `is_company_pan(vendor.pan)`; that function (apps/api/domain/tds/tds_computer.py:131-141) returns True for every PAN whose 4th character is not P or H, so 'F' (firm/LLP) and 'A'/'B' (AOP/BOI) and co-operatives all land in the foreign-company branch. The same boolean also selects `company_rate_bps=3500` for `other_sums` (domain/tds/section_195_rates.py:173-176) instead of the 30% non-corporate rate. Part II of the First Schedule gives a firm or a co-operative society a single 12% surcharge above ₹1 crore, which is neither of the two ladders held.
findings.ca_experience: On a ₹2 crore payment to a foreign partnership for 'other sums', the surcharge applied is 2% (foreign-company band) instead of 12%, and the base rate 35% instead of 30% — two errors in opposite directions that do not cancel. Under-withholding on a foreign remittance disallows the WHOLE expenditure under §40(a)(i), which the module's own docstring (section_195.py:38-42) names as the reason this matters more than a rounding error.
findings.market_standard: Not a comparison point — no mass-market Indian product computes §195 well; this module is already ahead of them. The defect is internal.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the `is_company` boolean with a payee-class enum derived from the PAN's 4th character (individual/HUF, firm/LLP, AOP/BOI, company, co-operative, trust) and hold one surcharge ladder per class, plus the correct 'other sums' rate per class. Confidence is medium because the FY 2025-26 Part II ladders are quoted from knowledge rather than from a source in this repo — and `section_195_rates.py:210-213` already records that every year is `verified=False`, so this belongs in the same line-by-line confirmation pass.

findings.title: tds_section_limits ships seeded with pre-Finance-Act-2025 thresholds and pre-2024 rates, and its aggregate §194C row is silently dropped
findings.evidence: apps/api/migrations/037_tds_engine.sql:122-141 inserts `('194J', ..., 30000_00, 10, 10)`, `('194I', ..., 240000_00, 10, 10)`, `('194H', ..., 15000_00, 5, 5)`, `('194D', ..., 15000_00, 5, 10)`, `('194A', ..., 4000_00, ...)` — every one superseded. The table's primary key is `section` (:113) and two rows are inserted for '194C' (:127-128, single and aggregate) under `ON CONFLICT (section) DO NOTHING` (:141), so the ₹1,00,000 aggregate row never lands. grep across apps/api and apps/web for 'tds_section_limits' returns zero readers, and it carries a `FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (true)` policy (:166-169) that exposes it firm-wide.
findings.ca_experience: Nothing today — nothing reads it. But it is a loaded trap: it is the one table in the schema that looks like the authoritative TDS rate master, it is world-readable to any authenticated user, and the next person who writes a report or a dropdown against it will ship FY 2019-era thresholds with no test failing.
findings.market_standard: n/a — internal data hygiene.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the table in a migration, or add a comment on it pointing at `domain/tds/section_rates.py` as the authority and a test that asserts it has no readers. Do not update the figures in place — that creates the second source of truth CLAUDE.md's posting-kernel rule exists to prevent.

findings.title: The 26Q/24Q from-books flow makes the CA re-type the TAN, deductor name, PAN and address every quarter, and validates the TAN only by length
findings.evidence: apps/api/routers/tds.py:98-106 (`FromBooksRequest`) requires `tan`, `deductor_name`, `deductor_pan`, `deductor_address` from the caller; apps/web/app/clients/[id]/compliance/tds/page.tsx:331 initialises all four to empty strings and :462 has the CA type the TAN. Yet migration 325 created `client_statutory_identity.tan` with a real format CHECK (`apps/api/migrations/325_a_client_has_its_own_statutory_registrations.sql:90`) precisely for this — its own header at :20 says 'The visible consequence is routers/tds.py: Compute24QRequest takes `tan`'. That table is read only by payroll (apps/api/routers/payroll.py:3609, :3698). Validation is weak too: `_validate_26q` (apps/api/domain/tds/tds_computer.py:331-332) checks `len(payload.tan) != 10` while `TDSValidator.validate_tan` with the real `^[A-Z]{4}[0-9]{5}[A-Z]$` regex (domain/tds/tds_validator.py:11, :21-23) is never called on it.
findings.ca_experience: Four fields re-typed per client per quarter per form — for a firm with forty clients that is 640 keystrokes of statutory identity a year, each of them an opportunity to key a wrong TAN that the length check will happily accept ('1234567890' passes). A wrong TAN on a filed statement is a correction statement.
findings.market_standard: Every TDS product holds the deductor master — TAN, name, address, responsible person, designation, PAN — once per client and never asks again. Saral and Winman also validate the TAN check-format on entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Default the four fields from `client_statutory_identity` (adding deductor address and responsible-person columns there if absent) and let the CA override. Call `TDSValidator.validate_tan` in `_validate_26q`/`_validate_24q` instead of the length check.

verification.what_is_actually_true: The four deductor fields are request-body inputs the CA retypes each quarter (apps/api/routers/tds.py:98-105; apps/web/app/clients/[id]/compliance/tds/page.tsx:331,:461) even though migration 325 created client_statutory_identity.tan with the real format CHECK at :90 for exactly this purpose and says so at :20-25, and that table is read only by payroll (apps/api/routers/payroll.py:3609,:3698). findings.title: The browser-built return reports every deduction as fully deposited, so the 'deducted exceeds deposited' validation can never fire
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/tds/returns/page.tsx:121: `tds_deposited_paise: Number(d.tds_paise ?? 0)` — the deposited amount is set equal to the deducted amount for every deductee, unconditionally, regardless of whether any challan exists. apps/api/domain/tds/tds_computer.py:347-352 then computes `gap = total_tds_deducted_paise - total_tds_deposited_paise` and raises 'TDS deducted (₹X) exceeds deposited — Challan 281 deposit required' only when `gap > 0`, which by construction is never. The server-side `from-books` path does this correctly, apportioning real challan totals (apps/api/services/tds_return_service.py:200-209).
findings.ca_experience: The one validation on the return that would tell a CA 'you have not deposited this quarter's TDS yet' is disabled on the screen that is labelled 'Prepare a Return'. The summary shows total deducted and total deposited as identical figures and a clean validation list, on a quarter where nothing has been paid to the Government.
findings.market_standard: Every TDS product refuses to build the statement until deductions are mapped to challans and the totals tie; the FVU enforces it too.
findings.suggested_fix: Falls out of TDS-03's fix — delete the browser-side assembly and use `/26q/from-books`, which reads real challans. If the screen must survive in the interim, set `tds_deposited_paise` from the matched challan or leave it at 0.

verification.what_is_actually_true: apps/web/app/tds/returns/page.tsx:124 sets every deductee's `tds_deposited_paise` equal to its `tds_paise`, so `total_tds_deposited_paise` always equals `total_tds_deducted_paise` (apps/api/domain/tds/tds_computer.py:189-190) and the 'TDS deducted exceeds deposited — Challan 281 deposit required' error at :348-352 is unreachable from that screen; the same screen shows both totals as identical. The server-side /26q/from-books path is correct (apps/api/services/tds_return_service.py:194-209). Severity stays medium rather than high because the same page also ships a placeholder TAN and deductor PAN (:144,:151), so its output is a misleading summary, not a filable statement.
verification.probe: `python -c` against TDSComputer.compute_26q with one ₹5,00,000 §194J deductee and no challans: browser shape (deposited := deducted) printed `deducted 5000000 deposited 5000000 errors [] warnings []`; the honest shape (deposited = 0) printed `errors ['TDS deducted (₹50000) exceeds deposited — Challan 281 deposit required']`. The validation fires only when the payload is built the way the browser never builds it.

lens_notes.literal: Confirmed; the cited line is :124, not :121. apps/web/app/tds/returns/page.tsx:123-124 builds each deductee with `tds_deducted_paise: Number(d.tds_paise ?? 0)` immediately followed by `tds_deposited_paise: Number(d.tds_paise ?? 0)` — the same source value, unconditionally, with no reference to any challan. apps/api/domain/tds/tds_computer.py:189-190 sums those two fields into the payload totals, so the totals are equal by construction, and :348-352 raises the 'exceeds deposited' error only when `gap > 0`. The challan list the page also sends (:130-141) is stored on the payload at :186 (`payload.challans = challans`) and never enters the deposited total. The server-side from-books path does it properly at apps/api/services/tds_return_service.py:194-209, apportioning the real deposited challan total per section via `apportion` and capping it at what was deducted.

findings.title: Nothing computes what TDS is due for deposit this month, so there is no challan-281 worksheet to pay from
findings.evidence: `tds_deductions` rows carry `transaction_date` and `quarter` but no deposit-period grouping, and no endpoint aggregates them by deduction month. `POST /api/tds-workspace/challans` (apps/api/routers/tds_workspace.py:261-310) takes an amount the CA types in and books the whole of it as `tds_paise` with `total_paise` equal to it and `interest_paise`/`penalty_paise` left at their defaults; `minor_head` is fixed at '200' by the column default (apps/api/migrations/037_tds_engine.sql:72) with no way to record a 400 (regular assessment) deposit. `compliance_engine.tds_deposit_due_date` (apps/api/services/compliance_engine.py:292-306) computes the correct 7th/30-April rule and is called only from `payroll_deposit_due_dates`.
findings.ca_experience: On the 5th of the month the CA has to work out, per client and per section, how much TDS was deducted last month and is due by the 7th. The platform holds every deduction row and will not add them up for them. They export to Excel — the exact workflow the product exists to replace.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime's 'TDS Outstanding' and Saral's challan worksheet both group deductions by deposit month and section, add §201(1A) interest where late, and print the challan 281 values (section code, minor head, TDS/surcharge/education cess/interest/fee split) ready for e-Pay Tax.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `GET /api/tds-workspace/deposit-due?client_id&month` that groups `tds_deductions` by (section, deduction month) into a challan-281 worksheet with the due date from `compliance_engine.tds_deposit_due_date` and interest from TDS-08's new module, then let the CA create the challan from that worksheet with the split pre-filled rather than typing one number.

verification.what_is_actually_true: Nothing in the product aggregates tds_deductions by deduction month into a challan-281 worksheet: no such endpoint exists on routers/tds.py or routers/tds_workspace.py, `compliance_engine.tds_deposit_due_date` (services/compliance_engine.py:292-306) is wired only into payroll (:326), the quick-create challan at routers/tds_workspace.py:261-310 books one typed number as pure TDS with minor_head pinned to '200' by migrations/037_tds_engine.sql:71, and no §201(1A) interest module exists. The one tile that looks like an answer, apps/web/app/tds/page.tsx:456,:551, counts challans with a blank BSR code instead. This is a real gap, and the backend-exists-but-unreachable escape does not apply — the backend does not have it either.

findings.title: Purchase debit and credit notes never reverse TDS, so a return after deduction leaves the register and the 26Q overstated
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/tds_return_service.py:33-37 states it plainly: 'purchase debit/credit notes never adjust tds_paise in this codebase (confirmed — routers/debit_notes.py and routers/purchase_credit_notes.py never touch it), so a purchase return after TDS was already deducted and deposited is not modelled here either.' Confirmed: the 26Q builder reads only `purchase_bills` (`_posted_vendor_tds_bills` at :132-137) and no note table. `sync_for_bill` (apps/api/services/tds_register_service.py:128) is keyed on `purchase_bill_id` and has no note counterpart.
findings.ca_experience: A ₹5 lakh §194J bill is booked, ₹50,000 withheld and deposited. The vendor then issues a credit note for ₹2 lakh. The 26Q still reports a ₹5 lakh payment with ₹50,000 TDS, and the vendor's 26AS shows credit on income they did not earn. The CA has to adjust it outside the system, and the books-to-GL reconciliation on the return (:290-296) will still say 'matched' because the GL was never adjusted either.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime reverses the TDS on a purchase return through its 'TDS Adjustment' voucher and carries the adjustment into the quarterly return; Zoho Books nets the credit note against the deduction.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the policy first — a credit note in the same quarter reduces the deduction, one after deposit becomes an excess-deposit adjustment carried to the next quarter — then implement it in the register and the 26Q builder. It is an accounting decision as much as a coding one.

verification.what_is_actually_true: Purchase debit and credit notes carry no TDS handling at all — apps/api/routers/debit_notes.py and apps/api/routers/purchase_credit_notes.py contain no occurrence of 'tds' in any case — and the 26Q builder reads only posted purchase_bills with tds_paise > 0 (apps/api/services/tds_return_service.py:132-137), while the register syncs per purchase_bill_id only (apps/api/services/tds_register_service.py:128,:163,:218). A purchase return after deduction leaves both the register and the 26Q overstated, and the books-vs-GL reconciliation at :289-296 still reports 'matched' because neither side moved.

The 26Q builder's population is `_posted_vendor_tds_bills` at :132-137, a single `purchase_bills` query filtered on `tds_paise > 0` and bill_date; no note table appears anywhere in the module. `sync_for_bill` (services/tds_register_service.py:128) keys its register row on `purchase_bill_id` (the delete at :163, the upsert at :218) and there is no note-shaped counterpart in the file.

maturity.rationale: Two very different halves. The DOMAIN LAYER is among the strongest work in this repo: domain/tds/section_195.py asks chargeability before rate and cites GE India Technology Centre; residency.py transcribes the resident-only charging words from the Act rather than inferring them; vocabulary.py forks the 1961 and 2025 Acts by event date and refuses the s.393 payment codes rather than inventing them; form26as_matcher.py is a genuinely good four-pass identity-first reconciler that reports the Rule 37BA(1) direction most tools ignore; and 446 tests across sixteen TDS test modules pass. But the PIPELINE from that domain layer to a CA's desk is broken in several independent places at once. The core resident computation under-deducts on every repeat vendor because only §194C has an FY-aggregate threshold (TDS-01), and over-deducts six-fold on §194Q (TDS-02). The one screen called 'Prepare a Return' cannot produce a return in production — no auth header, NULL financial_year, mismatched quarter format (TDS-03). Form 16A creation always fails silently against the real database (TDS-04). The /tds screen computes TDS in the browser off a stale rate table and writes straight to the database past rbac (TDS-05, TDS-11). There is no 27Q builder, no TCS at all, no §201(1A) interest, no §234E fee, no §197 certificate, no FVU output and no correction statement. Grade C rather than D because the foundations that are hard to build are right and the things that are wrong are mostly fixable in days, and grade C rather than B because a CA using this today would compute wrong withholding on ordinary domestic vendors — the most common case, not the exotic one.
maturity.would_a_ca_buy_this_module_alone: No — a TDS product a CA buys is one that produces an FVU-ready statement, computes §201(1A) interest and §234E fee, handles §197 certificates and maps deductions to challans, and this does none of those while also under-deducting on any vendor billed repeatedly below the section threshold.

open_questions_for_owner: Do you want the /tds top-level screen (browser-computed TDS, unpersisted challans, stale rate table) fixed or deleted? The per-client /clients/[id]/compliance/tds screen already calls the real API for almost everything it does, and keeping two TDS screens is how the two rate tables diverged in the first place. Deleting it is the cheaper and safer answer, but it is the only screen with a CSV import of deductions.

Is the FVU/RPU text-file writer in scope? It is the single feature that decides whether a CA buys the TDS module alone, it is months of work per form per FY, and everything else on this list is comparatively cheap. If it is not in scope, the honest positioning of this module is 'computes and reconciles TDS; you file in the free NSDL RPU' — which is defensible but should be said out loud on the screen.

Is TCS in or out? Section 206C(1H) affects any trading client with a buyer over ₹50 lakh, which is a large share of the SME book the platform targets, and it is entirely absent. It is a distinct build (collection on receipt, 27EQ, Form 27D), not a data-registry gap.

How should the §194J/§194H/§194A crossing bill behave once aggregate thresholds are modelled? The statute requires TDS on the whole aggregate once it is crossed, which means the crossing bill withholds more than its own 10% — that is correct but surprising, and it changes the vendor's net payable. Does that need a CA confirmation step, or should it just happen?

Do you want §197 lower-deduction certificates as a first-class master (number, rate, validity, ceiling, consumption tracking) or is honouring vendors.tds_rate_bps as a manual override enough for now? The current state — a rate the CA can type that the engine ignores — is the worst of the three.

The §195 rate registry is verified=False for every year and the resident registry is unverified for FY 2026-27, while today is 07-09-2026 and FY 2026-27 is live. Who is doing the Finance Act line-by-line confirmation, and by when? The fallback returns last year's figures confidently, which is the trap CLAUDE.md already names.

The tds_deductions register is written by two independent paths (the purchase-bill sync, and the browser) with different quarter formats and different completeness. Should the register become bill-only, with manual deductions entered as a document, or does it need to stay a free-standing register for TDS on rent, interest and journal-only payments that never reach a purchase bill? That decision determines whether the from-books 26Q builder or the register-based one is the right foundation.
strengths: domain/tds/section_195.py asks the questions in the statutorily correct ORDER — chargeability, then nature, then treaty, then PAN, then surcharge and cess — and refuses rather than guessing on the three that matter (no nature recorded, business profits with no no-PE declaration, a TRC on file with no treaty rate). It cites GE India Technology Centre (P) Ltd v. CIT (2010) 327 ITR 456 at :6-12 for why an ordinary import withholds nil rather than 20%. Nothing else in the Indian mass market gets this right.

domain/tds/residency.py:159-175 transcribes the 'to a resident' charging words of each of the twelve resident-only sections from the Act itself, and lists §194B separately at :181 because it charges 'to any person' — so the classification can be checked without leaving the file, and a future §194E is classified by reading rather than by pattern-matching. The refusal at :271-306 stops a resident section being recorded against a non-resident payee.

domain/tds/vocabulary.py forks the 1961 and 2025 Acts by EVENT date rather than migrating (:19-29), refuses to name a form without a period (:358-364), refuses the reverse s.393(1)→194-series map because it would have to invent one (:254-272), and refuses the sixty-seven s.393 payment codes outright (:282-301) rather than guessing them. Both vocabularies are permanent, which is correct — a belated FY 2025-26 return is Form 24Q for ever.

domain/income_tax/form26as_matcher.py:312-433 is a well-built reconciler: four passes strongest-identity-first (TAN+amount, name+amount, TAN, name), each consuming the credits it matches so no book credit is claimed twice, deterministic tie-breaking by date proximity, and — the part most tools miss — it reports the books→26AS direction and names it under Rule 37BA(1) as credit that is not claimable until the deductor corrects. TRACES booking status is honoured, with a blank status treated as NOT final (:121-130).

domain/payroll/form24q.py applies the 2025-Act vocabulary at the LINE level, not just the header (:164-165), and its challan filter deliberately accepts both the old and the new section label (:172-180) because 'a challan records what somebody typed, not which Act governs the quarter'. Its CSV working paper writes the missing payment-code gap and every readiness problem INTO the file (:315-330), so a downloaded document outlives the toast that warned about it.

services/tds_return_service.py reconciles the computed 26Q/24Q total to the GL 'TDS Payable' control account through the SPECIFIC journal entries the source documents posted rather than a date-range scan (:108-129, with the reasoning at :16-23), resolves the account by exact name to avoid the 'TDS Payable' / 'TDS Payable - Salary' substring ambiguity (:82-105), and pages every query with keyset paging so a client over 1,000 rows is not silently truncated (:60-79).

The TDS base is the taxable amount excluding GST by construction, not by a separate rule: purchase_bills passes `total_taxable` into resolve_tds and the register writes `taxable_amount_paise` (services/tds_register_service.py:230 with the CBDT Circular 23/2017 citation at :31-35), so the book and the return agree because they read the same number.

The DTAA table is modelled as a firm-level (country, nature) reading rather than a per-vendor field (services/treaty_rate_service.py:278-289 explains why the vendor column was wrong), ships empty and is never seeded, treats 'no article' as an ANSWER rather than a missing rate, and REFUSES rather than falling back to the Act rate when a TRC is on file with no rate recorded. The settings screen (apps/web/app/settings/treaty-rates/page.tsx) is reachable from Settings, validates one-thing-per-row server-side, and carries zero business logic.

apps/web/app/accounting/suppliers/page.tsx is the model the rest of the frontend should follow — it loads the section list from GET /api/tds/sections (:186) and computes the amount via POST /api/tds/compute-amount passing the PAN so is_company and §206AA are derived server-side (:135-145), rather than hardcoding anything.

446 tests pass across sixteen TDS-related modules (run in this session), including a bill-level engine test that proves the individual-vs-company rate split by PAN 4th character, a vendor-residency/27Q test, a register-follows-the-bill test that asserts a cancelled bill loses its row, and a real-Postgres upsert test.

§206AA is enforced on the ACTUAL withheld amount, not merely as a post-hoc warning (domain/tds/tds_computer.py:309-310, wired from routers/purchase_bills.py:340-343), and the §206AA(7)/Rule 37BC non-resident carve-out that residents do not get is implemented and gated on the six particulars actually being held (domain/tds/section_195.py:234-245, routers/purchase_bills.py:385-393).

Every threshold and rate lookup is keyed on the FY the BILL falls in, not today (routers/purchase_bills.py:324-337, :399-408), so a bill entered late for a prior year uses that year's law — and the response carries `rates_verified` so a firm can see when it is withholding on carried-forward figures (routers/tds.py:352-368, plus a dedicated /rate-coverage endpoint at :393).
