What is well covered: the §195 decision order and its refusals; the vocabulary fork in both directions with its two deliberate refusals; the per-bill individual-vs-company rate split by PAN 4th character; the register's create/update/remove lifecycle across bill status transitions; the 26AS matcher's four passes and one-to-one consumption; client-assignment scope on every TDS route. What is NOT covered, and where the bugs live: (1) no test exercises an FY aggregate for any section but §194C, which is why TDS-01 survives — test_tds_section_rates asserts thresholds exist and are non-negative, never that a second bill crossing the annual limit deducts; (2) no test asserts §194Q computes on the excess (TDS-02); (3) nothing tests that sync_for_bill writes financial_year, so TDS-03's NULL column is invisible; (4) every certificate test uses mock mode with 'Form 16A', while the single real-Postgres insert uses '16A' — the constraint mismatch of TDS-04 falls exactly in the gap between them (tests/test_phase3_tds.py:111 vs tests/test_gst_tds_schema_drift_pg.py:291); (5) there is no test of any apps/web TDS screen at all — no test would notice that compute26Q sends no Authorization header, that the challan modal never persists, or that the certificates tab reads columns that do not exist; (6) the one test written to catch unguarded direct writes (tests/test_direct_write_tables_are_role_guarded.py) has a regex whose 400-character tail cap makes it miss both tds_deductions inserts and the tds_returns upsert — I reproduced this by running the module's own _direct_write_tables(), which returns 21 tables and no tds_* table while '.insert(' appears twice in app/tds/page.tsx. One test asserts a statutory behaviour that is no longer law: tests/test_tds_engine.py:327-338 pins §206AB's doubled non-filer rate, omitted by the Finance Act 2025 from 01-04-2025 (see TDS-24; medium confidence on the omission, high confidence that the function is FY-blind and unwired). No test covers §201(1A), §234E, TCS, 27Q assembly or challan-to-deduction mapping, because none of those exist.
what_exists:
Backend. domain/tds/ holds six modules. section_rates.py is an FY-versioned registry (FY 2025-26 verified against the Finance Act 2025, FY 2026-27 carried forward) of fifteen sections in integer basis points, plus quarter_dates() deriving Rule 31A period and due dates from any FY label. tds_computer.py is the single resolution point: resolve_tds() applies the threshold, the individual-vs-company rate by PAN 4th character and the §206AA no-PAN floor, and builds 24Q/26Q payload objects with validation errors and warnings. tds_validator.py holds PAN/TAN regexes and §206AA/§206AB rate helpers. residency.py routes a deduction to 26Q or 27Q under Rule 31A(4), lists the resident-only charging sections verbatim, and defines six named statutory gaps with CA-readable messages. section_195.py and section_195_rates.py compute withholding on a payment to a non-resident by nature of income under s.115A and Part II of the First Schedule, apply §90(2) against a recorded treaty rate, add surcharge and cess, honour the §206AA(7)/Rule 37BC carve-out, and refuse in three defined cases. vocabulary.py forks the 1961 and 2025 Act form and section names by event date (24Q→138, 26Q→140, 27Q→144, 27EQ→143, 192→392, 194-series→393(1), 195→393(2), 206C→394, Form 16→130, 16A→131, 26AS→168, 15G/15H→121) and names the s.393 payment-code table as an unheld gap.

Routers: /api/tds (26q and 24q compute from a caller payload, 26q and 24q from-books, compute-amount, sections, rate-coverage, returns and deductions listings, and CRUD for the firm's DTAA treaty rates); /api/tds-workspace (dashboard, deductions, challans, returns with a status ladder pending→prepared→ca_approved→filed gated on an explicit CA confirmation, a PRN and Manager+, certificates, and a deductor-side 26AS comparison); /api/form-26as (upload, parse from pasted text, list, reconcile, get). Services: tds_return_service builds 26Q from posted purchase bills and 24Q from finalised payroll runs and reconciles each to its GL control account through the specific journal entries the documents posted, excluding non-resident payees and reporting them; tds_register_service keeps tds_deductions in step with every purchase bill, including a nil §195 remittance, and returns named statutory gaps; treaty_rate_service resolves a (country, nature) DTAA position with a per-vendor override. domain/income_tax/form26as_service.py + form26as_matcher.py reconcile the client's own 26AS against the TDS-receivable leg of its receipts in both directions. Tables: tds_deductions (014, +037, +263, +307, +308, +309, +312), tds_returns, tds_challans, tds_certificates, tds_section_limits (037), dtaa_treaty_rates (310), form_26as_uploads/records/reconciliations (052, 291).

Frontend. /tds (four tabs: deductions, challans, returns, certificates), /tds/returns (prepare, approve, mark filed, download JSON, filing-demo wizard), /clients/[id]/compliance/tds (six tabs including compute-from-books and a 26AS comparison), /clients/[id]/tax/26as (upload, parse, reconcile), /settings/treaty-rates. Vendor TDS settings, residency, nature of income, TRC, Form 10F and no-PE declaration live on the vendor form under /clients/[id]/purchases.
